title: Comparison
description: The verdict of one run against a baseline. `inconclusive` is a first-class outcome: with stochastic decoding a single run pair cannot distinguish improvement from noise, and rounding toward a decision manufactures exactly the false confidence this subsystem exists to prevent.

refusal_reason.description: Required when verdict is refused. The comparator refuses rather than reporting a number when the two runs are not comparable: differing attribution tuples, unequalized detectors, a declared protocol that does not match the data structure, or a suite whose case count is below the exact test support, so that no outcome it could ever produce would be significant.

test.description: Named per suite type and recorded, not improvised per comparison. Consensus practice for paired binary outcomes on a shared prompt set is McNemar on the discordant pairs, or 5x2 cross-validation with a modified paired t-test; graded and free-form metrics use a paired bootstrap over resamples of the prompt set. Different outcome types need different tests, and the choice is part of the result.

effective_n.description: Independent units behind the p-value. Once perturbations group cases this is smaller than the case count -- 70 rows over 14 briefs is 14 questions asked five ways, and treating it as 70 makes every p-value smaller than the evidence supports.

alpha.description: Significance threshold AFTER any multiplicity correction. Record the corrected value, not the nominal one.

comparisons_in_family.description: How many comparisons this one belongs to. This is not bookkeeping: an optimizer generates comparisons by construction, so a search over 100 candidates at a nominal 0.05 expects roughly five spurious winners. Uncorrected, the optimizer manufactures improvement out of multiplicity alone — a Goodhart channel distinct from a writable evaluator or an undersized anchor.

confidence_interval.description: Lower and upper bound at 1-alpha, for bootstrap protocols where an interval is more informative than a threshold verdict.

discordant.description: Pairs on which the two runs disagreed. This is the exact sample size of a McNemar test -- concordant pairs contribute no information to it -- so a comparison over 3,400 cases with 4 disagreements is a test with n=4.

min_attainable_p.description: The smallest p-value this design could have produced, over every possible arrangement of the outcomes it observed. For the exact two-sided binomial it is min(1, 2*0.5^discordant) and depends on nothing but the discordant count. It is not observed power -- observed power is a monotone function of the p-value and says nothing new -- it is the support of the test statistic, which is a property of the design.

attainable.description: Whether min_attainable_p clears alpha. False means no arrangement of these outcomes could have been significant, so inconclusive here reports the instrument, not the effect. Distinguishing the two is the difference between we looked and saw nothing and we could not have seen anything, and a promotion gate that cannot tell them apart is not a gate.

equalization.description: Evidence that both runs' detectors had comparable recall, DERIVED from the two runs' measured recall blocks rather than asserted by a caller. This replaced a boolean in 1.0.0. The boolean was never computed anywhere — a summary readable without consulting evidence is a summary that gets read instead of the evidence, which is how the guard came to check nothing. Keeping it beside this object would have preserved that. Null since 2.3.0: a comparison over a detector-less outcome (a judge score, not a detector pass/fail) has nothing to equalize, and forcing a placeholder value here would be exactly the vacuous claim ADR-0016 already had to name once for position_randomized on single-candidate gradings — null means not applicable, never a fudged zero.

max_gap.description: Largest |recall_candidate - recall_baseline| across detectors. Per-detector, never averaged: one asymmetric detector is enough to manufacture the artifact, and averaging is what lets a bad instrument hide behind good ones. Null when recall was missing or unmeasurable, which is a refusal rather than a value.

gap_bound.description: Derived from the suite's own detectable_delta, not chosen. A pure recall artifact has magnitude f*(r_b - r_c) <= |delta_r| since f <= 1, so bounding the gap by detectable_delta bounds the artifact by it. Recorded rather than merely applied, so an old comparison stays auditable against the rule in force when it ran.

effective_recall.description: Minimum recall across every detector the suite uses, over BOTH runs. A comparison is only as sharp as the blunter of the two instruments producing it. Null when it could not be computed.

adjusted_resolution.description: detectable_delta / effective_recall. A blunter instrument must show a larger observed difference before it is believed, because attenuation removes discordant pairs — the evidence McNemar consumes — not just magnitude. Equals detectable_delta exactly when recall is 1, so a perfect instrument sees no change in behaviour. Null when effective_recall is unknown or 0.
